faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary for a 38-hour week?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by 38 (hours per week) and then by 52 (weeks per year). For example, $40/hour × 38 × 52 = $79,040 gross per year. This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates. Use our [the timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures.

faqs.q: What tax and super should I expect on my annual pay?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates apply: nil up to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. See our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for an estimate.

faqs.q: Is the average weekly earnings figure for NSW a good guide for teacher salary NSW?
faqs.a: No. The ABS average weekly earnings for full-time employees in New South Wales ($2,108.80 per week in May 2026) is an average across all occupations and industries, not a median for teachers. Teacher salaries are set by award or enterprise agreements, and you should check specific pay rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman or your employer. Our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page has more context.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay: The 38-Hour Week

Whether you're a teacher in New South Wales or any other worker, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential. The standard full-time working week in Australia is 38 hours, and most annual salary calculations assume 52 weeks of work. This article explains the conversion formula, the role of the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and superannuation – all while keeping the keyword **teacher salary NSW** in context.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks.

For a full-time employee working 38 hours each week, the formula becomes:

**Annual = hourly × 38 × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $50, your annual gross pay is $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800. This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for budgeting and comparing job offers.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many Australian employees are paid fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Weekly pay is hourly × 38. So fortnightly = (hourly × 38) × 2. Using the same $50/hour example: weekly = $1,900, fortnightly = $3,800.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage, which from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. This is the legal floor – most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. For teachers in NSW, the relevant award is typically the *Teachers (Public Sector) Award* or similar, which includes pay scales based on classification and experience. Always check the specific award rate rather than relying on averages.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate should include a 25% casual loading (unless your award specifies a different amount). When using our [the timesheet](/) calculator, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the calculator adds it for you.

Superannuation (super) is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% from 1 July 2026, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution. For example, if your annual gross salary is $80,000, your employer must pay $9,600 into your super fund, provided your earnings are below the cap.

### Tax and Medicare

For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 plus 45% on excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. This estimate does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Putting It Together: Teacher Salary NSW Context

When you search for **teacher salary NSW**, you may come across figures like the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for full-time employees in New South Wales. In May 2026, that average was $2,108.80 per week. **This is an average across all occupations and industries, not a median for teachers.** Teacher salaries vary widely by experience, location, and sector (public vs private). For a more accurate picture, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides or your enterprise agreement. Our [pay guides](/blog) page can help you find the right award.

### Example Calculation for a Teacher

Suppose a NSW teacher has an hourly rate of $45 under their award. Assuming a 38-hour week:
- Weekly gross: $45 × 38 = $1,710
- Fortnightly gross: $1,710 × 2 = $3,420
- Annual gross: $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920
- Super (12%): $10,670.40 paid on top
- Estimated tax (using 2026–27 rates, no HELP): approximately $18,367 (including Medicare) – use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise estimate.

Remember, this is a simplified estimate. Actual pay may include allowances, overtime, or salary packaging that changes the figures.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay calculated here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
